items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Because…J.J. Johnson, he’s not a young man. He signed good contracts, still is.

ctx.x: Do you feel any, not resentment, but just the irony of something like Columbia seeming to sign every young musician almost on the basis of youth. It seems that you have to be under 25, even if they’re of marginal talent but just the fact that they’re young and can play, I mean it’s not that they’re completely incompetent but they all sound alike, do you sort of resent the attention that’s been focused on this younger movement in jazz?

No, I don’t resent it. I never have been resentment of nobody who’s successful. But I do think they should make an allowance for anybody that’s got the talent whether they’re young or old. ‘Cause I hear some of these youngsters can’t play near as good as some of these old-timers.

In fact a lot of these youngsters are trying to play like the old-timers. No, I think that’s absolutely not fair to any musician to deny him the pleasure of success if he can play regardless of age. Because…J.J. Johnson, he’s not a young man. He signed good contracts, still is. Of course it is controlled by the youngsters. items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He still had some of the holdovers, like Sweets was still there – Harry "Sweets" Edison, that is.

ctx.x: . . . and had really [admired], in the Basie band.

Oh yeah. Unfortunately my hero wasn’t there. Lester Young wasn’t there. He had some monsters in Lester’s place in the person of Don Byas, a killer, killer saxophone player, and Illinois Jacquet. They all came along after Lester. He still had some of the holdovers, like Sweets was still there – Harry "Sweets" Edison, that is. I first met Joe Newman in Basie’s band. Dickie Wells was still there. I held Dickie Wells in very high esteem. Dickie Wells was a unique trombonist in that less is more. Simple is good. His…

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: That was Coleman Hawkins, Howard McGhee, Thad Jones, J.J. Johnson, Sonny Stitt, myself, Miles Davis.

ctx.x: Let's see, I took a trip to Europe with Basie in 1960, '62. 1962, I went with Basie. I went for three months and stayed a year, you know? And that's when Jaws* was with the band. We did some dates over there with Tony Bennett. Let's see, was that '62? I think it was, because my first trip to Europe was with the George Wein Newport thing. That was Coleman Hawkins, Howard McGhee, Thad Jones, J.J. Johnson, Sonny Stitt, myself, Miles Davis.
